correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts every factorization shape with \(\Omega(n)\le3\). Under \(\sigma(n)\mid n^2\), each prime-power divisor-sum factor has prime support contained in that of \(n\). Prime powers are eliminated by coprimality; \(pq\) forces \(p+1=q\) and hence \(6\); \(p^2q\) forces \(p=2,q=7\) and hence \(28\); and \(pqr\) forces \(p=2,q=3\), after which \(r+1\mid3\), impossible. The exact identity \(\sigma(364)=784\) and \(364^2=169\cdot784\) proves sharpness.

The theorem proves that only the perfect numbers \(6,28\) occur there and therefore determines the exact minimum multiplicity of a non-perfect member.
